question: how much does the registered do-nothing clause decide, on the declared 12-seed block, before its own data exists

readings.anchors_by_clause: the clause table was anchored on the one contrast that had been measured (the null clause's, z = 1.20); section 5.66 measured the other two at the same fidelity on fresh seeds under the declared policies, and ``dev_fidelity_anchors_by_clause`` now carries each clause's own contrast and the firing rate at it - so the declared verdict's three clauses are read against three measured analogues rather than one
readings.clauses_are_not_redundant: on section 5.40's dev-fidelity seeds the null clause fires (the null beats adaptive on 12/12) while the harm guard does not (the random arm beats it on 6/12), so a verdict can withhold on one clause and clear another; the third arm that block lacked is measured on the section 5.66 block, where each clause's own contrast is reported beside its firing rate
readings.modal_verdict: with the dev-fidelity effect (z = 1.20) the clause fires with probability 0.8483; since section 5.40 measured the null arm ahead on 12/12 fresh seeds, a withheld Gate 4 is the modal outcome and it is strong evidence, not a coin flip
readings.one_rule_three_arms: all three withhold clauses are the same 10-of-12 sign test on the adaptive arm, differing only in the comparison arm (random, pool-matched control, null); each has level 0.0193 and the union is at most 0.0579 by the union bound, less in fact because a hard block fires them together
readings.what_a_pass_is_worth: a pass needs only 3 of 12 seeds favouring the adaptive arm, and under no effect it happens with probability 0.9807 - so a cleared null clause is not evidence that adaptive beats doing nothing, and the verdict's value claim then rests on the registered cost/band/control rules exactly as registered
